title: Subsets
description:
Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set).
The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets. Return the solution in any order.
 
Example 1:

Input: nums = [1,2,3]
Output: [[],[1],[2],[1,2],[3],[1,3],[2,3],[1,2,3]]

Example 2:

Input: nums = [0]
Output: [[],[0]]

 
Constraints:

1 <= nums.length <= 10
-10 <= nums[i] <= 10
All the numbers of nums are unique.
starter_code:
class Solution:
    def subsets(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:

check_function:
def check(candidate):
    assert sorted(map(tuple, candidate(nums = [1,2,3]))) == sorted(map(tuple, [[],[1],[2],[3],[1,2],[1,3],[2,3],[1,2,3]]))
    assert sorted(map(tuple, candidate(nums = [0]))) == sorted(map(tuple, [[],[0]]))
    assert sorted(map(tuple, candidate(nums = [-1,1]))) == sorted(map(tuple, [[],[-1],[1],[-1,1]]))
    assert sorted(map(tuple, candidate(nums = [3,1]))) == sorted(map(tuple, [[],[3],[1],[3,1]]))
    assert len(candidate(nums = [1,2,3,4])) == 16
    assert sorted(map(tuple, candidate(nums = [-2,0,2]))) == sorted(map(tuple, [[],[-2],[0],[2],[-2,0],[-2,2],[0,2],[-2,0,2]]))
    assert () in map(tuple, candidate(nums = [5,6,7]))
    assert (5,6,7) in map(tuple, candidate(nums = [5,6,7]))
